short: Extraordinary mechanical properties of AZ61 alloy processed
title: Extraordinary mechanical properties of AZ61 alloy processed by ECAP with 160° channel angle and EPT

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Conventionally deformed or SPD-processed rare-earth-free AZ61 has unbalanced, moderate yield and tensile strength. High stored deformation energy from ECAP plus an instantaneous electropulse should complete static recrystallization fast, giving ultrafine grains and strength with ductility.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/route), n5 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/treatment), n11 (DES/down_select), n12 (PRC/treatment), n14 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: At 373 K, twins and deformation bands accumulate with passes up to 4 without dynamic recrystallization, storing deformation energy. Dynamic recrystallization refines grains at 423 K after 4-5 passes and at 473 K already after 3 passes.
states.detail: Absorbed: n7 (STR/defect/extended), n8 (STR/microstructure/feature_size), n13 (STR/microstructure/feature_size), n15 (STR/microstructure/feature_size). Premises: Fine equiaxed grains replacing twinned deformed grains mark recrystallization; retained twins and elongated grains mark incomplete recrystallization

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Yield strength rises with ECAP passes at 373 K to ~300 MPa at 4 passes; at 423 K it peaks (~230 MPa) at 4 passes then drops at 5. Low-temperature ECAP accumulates dislocations and stored energy (strengthening); DRX at 423 K-5 consumes it and lowers YS, so ECAP temperature controls stored energy.
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (PRP/value), n10 (MEC/pathway), n17 (MEC/pathway), n18 (PRP/value). Premises: Yield stress as sum of Hall-Petch grain-boundary, Mg17Al12 precipitation and dislocation strengthening terms

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: ECAP+EPT AZ61 lies above all compared AZ61 routes (ECAP, forging, rolling, casting, FSP) in both YS and UTS. Variable-temperature ECAP with a 160 deg die followed by short electropulsing gives ultrafine recrystallized AZ61 with 448 MPa UTS and 15% elongation
states.detail: Absorbed: n19 (DSC/comparison), n20 (DSC/conclusion). Premises: Literature AZ61 data (Table 4): conventional deformation and SPD routes give YS/UTS pairs used as comparators

nodes.title: evidence, F12, F15
nodes.head: YS rises monotonically 120-300 MPa over passes 1-4 for 373 K; 423 K rises 140-230 MPa to pass 4 then falls to 150 MPa at pass 5. 373K-4 curve reaches ~350 MPa but ends near 0.06 true strain; as-received peaks ~300 MPa at ~0.17
nodes.solves: Yield strength rises with ECAP passes at 373 K to ~300 MPa at 4 passes; at 423 K it peaks (~230 MPa) at 4 passes then drops at 5
nodes.note: text gives as-received UTS 260 MPa and TEF 16%; curve peak ~300 MPa (true vs engineering stress likely); 373K-4 text UTS 360 vs ~350 read

nodes.title: PROCESS, F10, F7, F9
nodes.head: After full recrystallization grain size ranks F10d (~1 um) < F7c (~5-8 um) < F9c (~15-30 um, with twinned remnants)
nodes.solves: The high stored energy of variable-temperature ECAP plus an instantaneous high-energy pulse lets recrystallization finish in a short time before grains grow
nodes.note: the three panels also differ in pulse parameters (F7c 30us-10min, F9c 40us-10min, F10d 25us-10min, captions), so the ranking conflates ECAP state with EPT dose
